headline: Govt says police cannot carry out crossfire even if ordered
summary: Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman clarifies that public servants are not obliged to obey unlawful instructions, following controversial remarks by the IGP.
details: Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Cultural Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government cannot order police to carry out ‘crossfire’, and officers cannot execute such an order as they are not obliged to obey unlawful instructions.
The remarks come after Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir recently suggested that police would resort to crossfire if necessary and permitted by the government.
Adviser Zahed noted that the IGP has since acknowledged the problem with his statement and has stepped back from his original position.
The adviser further mentioned that the the prime minister is currently abroad in Japan and will consider the government’s final position on the matter after returning home.
Regarding the return of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, Zahed said she would have to face justice according to the law and would not face mob violence.
He also addressed the rise of fundamentalism and the far right, stating that the government is taking these developments seriously and taking strict measures in response.
caption:
Can police carry out 'crossfire' if the government orders it? The government says no.

Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Cultural Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government cannot order police to carry out ‘crossfire’, and officers cannot execute such an order as they are not obliged to obey unlawful instructions.

The remarks come after Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir recently suggested that police would resort to crossfire if necessary and permitted by the government.

Adviser Zahed noted that the IGP has since acknowledged the problem with his statement and has stepped back from his original position.

The adviser further mentioned that the the prime minister is currently abroad in Japan and will consider the government’s final position on the matter after returning home.

Regarding the return of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, Zahed said she would have to face justice according to the law and would not face mob violence.

He also addressed the rise of fundamentalism and the far right, stating that the government is taking these developments seriously and taking strict measures in response.

#Bangladesh #Police #HumanRights #LawAndOrder #Governance

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: 400 deaths: [[Dengue death toll hits 400]] as October becomes deadliest month
headline: 400 deaths: Dengue death toll hits 400 as October becomes deadliest month
summary: Eleven more people died in 24 hours, with over 2,000 new hospital admissions across Bangladesh.
details: Eleven people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll for this year to 400, according to official figures.
A total of 2,071 patients were admitted to hospitals nationwide in a single day, with the Dhaka Division recording the highest number at 899 admissions.
October has emerged as the deadliest month of the year, with 155 deaths recorded in this month alone.
Regional admissions include 250 in Khulna, 241 in Chattogram, 229 in Rajshahi, 217 in Barishal, 112 in Rangpur, 97 in Mymensingh, and 26 in Sylhet.
So far this year, 128,237 dengue patients have been hospitalised across the country.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has been tracking these figures since 2000, noting that 2023 was the worst year on record with 1,705 deaths.
Last year, the disease claimed over 400 lives and resulted in more than 102,000 diagnosed cases.
